subject: Hightower pilot — availability concession & operational asks
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@hightower.ai>
To: elliot.price@redwood.com
Cc: priya@hightower.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hightower pilot — availability ask and runbook request

Hi Elliot,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the pilot went well. As we move to a two-week integration pilot, our ops team is asking whether Redwood can commit to an availability target for the pilot window. They're specifically requesting: a written acknowledgment of 99.9% monthly availability for the pilot and a basic operational runbook that outlines on-call escalation, incident contact, and blackout maintenance windows.

We know full enterprise SLAs are a bigger lift; for the pilot we just need a short, formalized commitment and a runbook so our compliance folks can greenlight the staging cutover.

Can you loop in the right folks and let us know what is feasible? Also, if you have a short SLA draft we can review, that would speed signoff.

Appreciate it — Samir
Head of Platform Integrations
Hightower.ai
From: elliot.price@redwood.com
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hightower pilot — availability ask and runbook request

Team — forwarding Hightower's ask. TL;DR: pilot-level written 99.9% monthly availability commitment + a concise operational runbook.

Key constraints from sales/CS:
- Pilot runs for 2 weeks starting 2026-09-21; low volume but enterprise tester workloads during PST business hours.
- Customer wants a signed acknowledgement (not full SLA doc) and a runbook for their auditors.

What I need from each of you:
- Grace: product/legal touchpoints — what language can we safely provide for a pilot-level pledge vs. a contract SLA?
- Marcus: ops/infra — can we produce a 1-page runbook with emergency contact + fallback plan? Any operational risks if we promise 99.9% for that window?
- Laura: commercial — will this require a concession/credit or special pricing note?

I've attached a quick draft I started (SLA_draft_Hightower_v0.3.docx) and a sample runbook template we can adapt. Feedback by EOD tomorrow would be great — Samir is keen to close this week.

[Attachment: SLA_draft_Hightower_v0.3.docx]
[Attachment: operational_runbook_hightower_v2.pdf]

Thanks — Elliot
Director, Strategic Accounts

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: elliot.price@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hightower pilot — availability ask and runbook request

Elliot — quick thoughts:

1) Language: For pilots we can offer a 'pilot availability acknowledgment' that states a target (99.9%) and clarifies that it is not a contractually backed SLA (no service credits). Legal prefers wording that frames it as an operational commitment for the pilot window, with escalation procedures and no amendment to the master services agreement. I can draft a 2-paragraph statement.

2) Scope: We should limit the scope to the pilot environment and test traffic patterns only. No synthetic or load test guarantees.

3) Safety nets: Recommend we include an automatic fallback to a lower-cost model variant in the event of degraded performance, and a requirement for the customer to notify Redwood prior to any planned load tests.

I can put together the pilot pledge language if Marcus gives the runbook bullets.

Grace
VP, Product
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, elliot.price@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hightower pilot — availability ask and runbook request

Putting ops perspective here. Short answers:
- Can we do a pilot runbook? Yes. I can produce a 1-page runbook with: monitoring endpoints (links), primary on-call contact, escalation timeline (0-15m ack, 15-60m mitigation steps), known fallback (route to smaller model + cache warmup), maintenance blackout window: none during pilot unless pre-notified.
- 99.9% target for two weeks? Technically feasible but noisy for short windows. We'll call it a 'targeted availability acknowledgement' and include language that availability is measured over the pilot window normalized to serviceable hours. We should avoid promising credits.

Operational risks/asks from infra:
- Need a small reserved burst pool for the pilot (N1 GPUs for 2 hours/day) to ensure warmup and KV cache priming. Cost estimate attached.
- Request an internal on-call rotation for the pilot week (I can nominate engineers, but will need LAURA's go-ahead to classify this as high-touch).

Attaching suggested runbook bullets and a brief ops cost note.

[Attachment: operational_runbook_hightower_v2.pdf]
[Attachment: pilot_reserved_capacity_costs.xlsx] (stub)

Marcus
Director, Reliability Engineering

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: elliot.price@redwood.com, grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hightower pilot — availability ask and runbook request

Thanks for the quick turn. Summary and decision:
- Product/legal: draft 'pilot availability acknowledgement' (Grace) — acceptable. No credits.
- Ops: 1-page runbook + small reserved burst pool (Marcus) — approve the limited reservation for the pilot; treat as one-time operational expense to be absorbed by the strategic accounts bucket.
- Commercial: Elliot to present the acknowledgement + runbook to Hightower and confirm scope/measurement. If Hightower requests any further escalation (formal SLA & credits) we will escalate to finance/CS and treat as a commercial concession requiring approval.

Elliot — proceed with the note to the customer. Please copy me on the acknowledgement and attach the runbook. I'll record the internal exception and tag it to deal HTWR-2026-PILOT-42.

Laura
Senior Manager, Strategic Accounts

From: elliot.price@redwood.com

Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.com, marcus.lin@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hightower pilot — availability concession & operational asks

Samir / Priya — thanks for the ask and for the patience while we scoped this internally.

Attached: a short 'Pilot Availability Acknowledgement' (two paragraphs) and a 1-page operational runbook that covers on-call, escalation timeline, fallback behavior, and monitoring endpoints. Key points:
- Pilot commitment: Redwood will target 99.9% availability for the pilot window (2026-09-21 to 2026-10-05) for the agreed test traffic. This is an operational acknowledgement for pilot purposes only and is not a contract amendment or a service-credit-backed SLA.
- Scope/limits: Applies only to the pilot environment and normal test traffic; please notify us prior to any deliberate load tests.
- Operational support: We will allocate a small reserved burst pool and an on-call rotation for the pilot week. The runbook lists primary contacts and escalation steps.

Next steps: please review the attached documents and confirm you are OK with the wording and the measurement window. If you need formal SLA language with credits, we can explore a commercial concession with finance but that will take longer.

[Attachment: SLA_draft_Hightower_v0.3.docx]
[Attachment: operational_runbook_hightower_v2.pdf]

Best — Elliot
